clue.text: Setter's a feeder and 'e's to be a drinker

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, and 'Setter's' stands for 'I'm' (I am)
a feeder is a baby's bib, worn at mealtimes
'e is a dropped-aitch 'he', leaving just the letter E

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be a baby's bib, while some cockney fellow is going to be a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' gives I'M; the 's after 'e reads as 'is' and supplies no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, so 'to be a drinker' describes the verb's action.

clue.text: Russian front takes one over

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'over' puts the piece for one above the piece for front

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the van is the front of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A Russian army front advances and overruns a single soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link; 'over' places I on top of VAN in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a stock Russian first name, used for a Russian generally.

clue.text: Banks secondly on return of soldier to old city

parts.note: B is the second letter, as in grade B or 'plan B' being the second option

indicators.note: 'return of' turns back the words 'of soldier' together

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Banks, it seems, are next in line when a soldier comes back to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition. 'return' turns the two words 'of soldier' together, as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Four were the four dominant UK high-street banks, so the phrase names a group of banks.

clue.text: Sweet success

definitions.meaning: a hard, round, striped peppermint candy sold in Britain
a hit on the centre of a target, hence any direct success

explanation.definitionFit: A bull's-eye is both a British boiled mint and the target's centre, hence a hit.

clue.text: Capri lot could be from its corn

indicators.note: these letters could be something else if rearranged, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A heap of goods on Capri might have come from the island's own maize harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its corn' completes 'Capri' as Capricorn: the Tropic of Capricorn, so something from it is of the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropic of Capricorn is one of the two tropics, so anything from it relates to the hot equatorial belt.

clue.text: True Catholics with true characters change the system of …

indicators.note: the letters are taken as loose characters to be rearranged

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic, so Catholics are RCs

explanation.surface: Faithful Catholics with honest natures want to reform the system run by their church.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE + RCS + TRUE are rearranged by 'characters'. The ellipsis carries the sentence into 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To restructure something is to reorganise it, changing the system on which it runs.

clue.text: … their leader, the old spinach-eater

parts.note: following 5 down, the leader of the Catholics is the Pope
ye is an archaic spelling of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'

explanation.surface: The head of the Catholic Church is revealed as a spinach eater of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor is the cartoon character famous for gaining strength from eating spinach.

clue.text: Row 100 for "The Love of Paris"

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
in French, the language of Paris, 'the love' is l'amour

explanation.surface: A row of a hundred people queues for a film called The Love of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link here. Row is the noisy quarrel sense, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A row (rhyming with 'cow') is a loud dispute, synonymous with an uproar.

clue.text: For permit to enter toilet work outside digit

indicators.note: the piece for permit is to go into the rearranged word
the letters of toilet are worked into a new order

parts.note: to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A permit is needed to use the lavatory, while working out in the open hurts a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link, and 'outside' only restates that the rearranged lavatory word surrounds the permit.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest toe is a digit of the foot.

clue.text: Chancellor's fury about halt — end of work — on railway

indicators.note: the word for fury goes about, or around, the word for halt

parts.note: fury is anger
halt is an old word for lame, limping

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word work

parts.note: EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: The German leader is furious about a halt to work on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halt' here is the old adjective meaning limping, not a stop. The 's after Chancellor reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela Merkel was Chancellor of Germany from 2005 to 2021.

clue.text: Never, never split transverse stick

indicators.note: the word for transverse is split open to take the other piece

parts.note: aslant means slanting across, i.e. transverse
the never-never is British slang for hire purchase, abbreviated HP

explanation.surface: A stick that runs crossways must never, ever be split.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, buying 'on the never-never' means buying on hire purchase, paying in instalments; the comma makes 'Never, never' look like emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a walking stick cut from an ash sapling.

clue.text: Sweet companion not wanted by donkey

parts.note: a gooseberry is an unwanted third person with a courting couple
donkey is slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A companion is found unwelcome by a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. In Britain, 'playing gooseberry' means tagging along with a couple who want to be alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseberry fool is a British dessert of fruit purée folded into cream; British 'sweet' means pudding.

clue.text: Belinda's a striker without energy or vision

annotationWithheld.why: Belinda's a striker without energy or vision (5,2,1,3): BELINDAS + A + BAT less E, but 'without' is both the deletion indicator and needed in the definition 'without ... vision'
annotationWithheld.clue: Belinda's a striker without energy or vision

clue.text: Turn of one's own to stop political infighting, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: stopping fighting within a political party brings about party peace

explanation.surface: Someone does a turn of their own to end the bickering inside a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' indicates a sound-alike: PEACE and PIECE are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a performer's own habitual turn, trotted out at gatherings.

clue.text: Lunch for the homeward plodder

parts.note: a British pub lunch of bread, cheese and pickle bears the name of Gray's farm labourer who 'homeward plods his weary way'

explanation.walkthrough: Gray's Elegy opens with a farm worker plodding home; the classic British pub lunch is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure who plods homeward in Gray's Elegy is a farm labourer, and his name graces a cheese lunch.

clue.text: Left-wing movement

definitions.meaning: a Trotskyist, a member of the hard left
a jogging pace between walking and running

explanation.definitionFit: Trot is slang for a Trotskyist and also a horse's or runner's gait.

clue.text: Making a 7, start to scrap missile

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of scrap

parts.note: Trident is the submarine-launched nuclear missile

explanation.surface: Protesters make a noisy row when demanding a start to scrapping the missile.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 refers to 7 down, so 'making a 7' means making a clamour, being loud and harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh, which is what anyone causing a noisy outcry is being.

clue.text: Oven in which one has right to cook

annotationWithheld.why: Oven in which one has right to cook (4): A (one) + S (has) + TO rearranged would give the letters, but 'right' and 'in which' have no job and no source explains them
annotationWithheld.clue: Oven in which one has right to cook

clue.text: Big Apple for New York, my son?

definitions.text: Big Apple for New York, my son?

parts.words: Big Apple for New York, my son?
parts.note: the nickname stands in for the city's name, and the city's initials plus 'my son' scrambled make the word for such a stand-in

explanation.walkthrough: Big Apple is another name for New York; also NY + MY SON rearranged spell the answer, an anagram flagged only by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A word that can replace another with the same meaning, as one city nickname replaces its name.

clue.text: Not fixed a day? Managed it this very minute

parts.note: 'just' means at this very moment, as in 'he's just arrived'
if you managed it, you were able to

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a date can be moved and says they only just pulled it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adjustable can be altered or reset, so its position is not fixed.

clue.text: Connection in end of month to make horse see straight?

indicators.note: the word for connection is placed in the month ending

parts.note: September to December all end in -ber
a link is a connection

explanation.surface: Fit a connector at the end of the month so the horse can only look ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The month ending BER is a whimsical device.
explanation.definitionFit: A blinker is a leather flap restricting a horse's side vision so it looks only straight ahead; to blinker is to fit them.

clue.text: Non-21 description of Livingstone, say?

indicators.note: say signals a word heard rather than written

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, former Mayor of London, is a famous keeper of newts, so he could be called a newt-er

explanation.surface: A gender-neutral label for the explorer Livingstone, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Livingstone suggests the explorer, but it is Ken Livingstone, the London politician known for keeping newts. 21 is GENDER-SPECIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuter means of neither gender, so it is the opposite of being specific to one gender.

clue.text: Giving birth may be but feeding? Politically correct cries "Wrong!"

indicators.note: the cry of 'wrong' signals these letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Childbirth is limited to one sex but feeding is not, and the politically correct call that wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: FEEDING + PC + CRIES are rearranged; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Only women can give birth, so it is an activity belonging to one sex.

clue.text: Perform words and music of song on piano

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Performing a song's words and music on the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To play is to perform music or a part.

clue.text: Craze about to be part of province

indicators.note: the word for craze goes about the other pieces

parts.note: a craze is a mania
taken as written

indicators.note: part of takes just the first letter of be

explanation.surface: A craze is about to become part of the province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to', but it is the container signal; 'part of' takes just the B from 'be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the Canadian provinces.

clue.text: See 9
About return of bird — possibly a tern — that can count

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the turned bird
possibly signals the letters could be in another order
return of means the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Something about the return of a bird, maybe a tern, that has a head for figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A TERN to NRATE; 'return of' gives UME, which goes inside after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being numerate means being competent with numbers, able to count and calculate.

clue.text: Second to wait? It's like heaven

parts.note: to tarry is to wait or linger

explanation.surface: Wait a second, says someone; this feels like paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavens are full of stars, so starry means like the night sky.
